title: The 13 Best Toaster Ovens
metaDescription: Our 13 picks for toaster ovens, with key specs, strengths and limitations for each, based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.
lede: We looked at toaster ovens using manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. Each pick lists what it does well and where it falls short, so you can match it to how you'll use it.

products.name: Breville BOV800XL Smart Oven 1800-Watt Convection Toaster Oven
products.blurb: Key specs: Element IQ, five independently controlled heating elements, 1800W convection with 8 cooking functions, 0.8 cubic foot interior fits a 13x9 roasting pan or 12-inch pizza.
strengths: Element IQ produces the most even browning of any toaster oven, edge-to-edge on a full sheet of cookies
Thermostat holds within 5 to 15 degrees of the setting, versus a 50-degree spread on budget models
0.8 cubic foot cavity fits a 13x9 pan, a 12-inch pizza, or a whole 4-pound chicken
8 functions cover toast, bagel, bake, roast, broil, pizza, cookies, and reheat without gimmicks
limitations: No air fry function, the BOV900BSS is the air fry equivalent at a higher price
18.5-inch width requires a dedicated counter footprint
features: Element IQ, five independently controlled heating elements
1800W convection with 8 cooking functions
0.8 cubic foot interior fits a 13x9 roasting pan or 12-inch pizza
Thermostat accuracy within 5 to 15 degrees of the set point
Interior light for monitoring without opening the door

products.name: Cuisinart TOA-60 Air Fryer Toaster Oven
products.blurb: Key specs: 1800W with dedicated air fry setting and mesh Air Fryer Rack, 7 functions: air fry, convection bake, convection broil, bake, broil, warm, toast, 0.6 cubic foot cavity fits a 12-inch pizza.
strengths: Genuinely crispy air fry results, roughly 85-90% as crisp as a dedicated basket air fryer
0.6 cubic foot interior fits a 12-inch pizza while staying compact
3-year warranty beats the 1-year coverage on the Breville and most competitors
limitations: Thermostat runs 15°F to 25°F off the set temperature, requiring manual compensation for precise baking
No digital timer display in the base model, just a mechanical dial
Smaller cavity than the Breville, so a full 9x13 pan is tight
